summary: Private: request custom role to allow audit log export (SIEM) but deny billing access
environment: prod | private deployment (air-gapped) | customer region: us-east (customer DC)
description:
Customer request (Northstar Health, Private / air-gapped):

They need a role they can assign to their Security Operations team that can:
- View audit logs
- Export audit logs (download/export API or SIEM export config)

But MUST NOT be able to:
- View or modify billing settings
- View invoices/payment methods
- Change usage limits/commitments

Current state in their environment:
- Using RBAC v2 policy bundle v0.1 (defaults only).
- Closest default role is Security Admin, but it currently includes permissions that expose billing surfaces in Console (at least read-only).
- Billing Admin is obviously too broad for this user set.

Impact:
- Customer security review / go-live blocker for their Private rollout phase 2 (SOC monitoring requirements).

Ask:
- Provide recommended permission mapping and, if possible, a customer-safe way to implement a custom role in Private (given air-gapped constraints and signed artifacts).

Notes:
- Customer is fine with a short-term workaround (manual policy bundle update) if it is supportable and auditable.
- They requested written confirmation that billing access is not included in the proposed role (separation of duties).
comments:
2025-03-11 10:08 PT — Rachel Kim (CS) — Created ticket after customer email + call. Customer stakeholders: SecOps lead + IT admin. They referenced their internal SoD policy: "Security operations may access logs and exports but not financials." Asked whether Redwood supports custom roles in Private and how updates work in air-gapped environments.

Next step: pull in Security Eng + Audit Logging owner to confirm recommended permissions and whether export permission can be split from billing/usage surfaces.

2025-03-11 11:02 PT — Owen Phillips (Support) — Initial triage: confirmed this is Private and air-gapped. Their installer is pinned to 2025.02.2. They have Console enabled.

Observed in role matrix draft: some audit-related capabilities are currently bundled in Security Admin, but Console nav still shows Billing with read-only access depending on flags.

Escalating to Marcus Lin (Security) + Kevin Osei (Audit logging).

2025-03-11 13:26 PT — Marcus Lin (Security Eng) — Acknowledged. This is aligned with RBAC v2 separation-of-duties feedback we’ve been collecting.

Key point: in v0.1 policy bundle, audit log export is not cleanly separated from certain org-level administrative surfaces in the Console (depends on how endpoints are grouped).

Proposal:
- Introduce a custom role at customer: "Audit Log Exporter" (or "Audit Analyst") granting:
  - auditlog.read (list/view events)
  - auditlog.export (download/export endpoints)
  - auditlog.export_config.read/write (if they configure SIEM destinations)
- Explicitly exclude any billing.* and usage.* actions.

Need to verify action names in their policy bundle and whether export config is implemented as separate actions yet in Private build. Looping in Kevin + Chloe (Console backend).

2025-03-12 09:14 PT — Kevin Osei (Audit logging) — Confirmed desired separation is reasonable for SOC2/ISO evidence.

From our side, we want:
- auditlog.export to be a distinct sensitive action with clear audit events showing actor/role/policy_version.
- Export should emit an audit event (e.g., AUDIT_LOG_EXPORTED) with counts + filters (no payload).

We can support a customer custom role as long as:
- Policy bundle signature story is satisfied (Private packaging PR-219 covers signed artifacts).
- Customer accepts that this is an interim approach until custom roles are first-class in Console.

Requested: which method of export do they need (UI download vs API vs SIEM streaming).

2025-03-12 10:37 PT — Chloe Martin (Console backend) — In current Console backend, billing surfaces are guarded by billing.* actions. Audit log screens and download/export endpoints are guarded by auditlog.* actions, but there is one shared org settings endpoint that Security Admin hits for "audit log retention" display.

For this customer role, we can avoid that dependency and keep it purely auditlog.* if they don’t need retention changes.

If they need SIEM destination config, that is under auditlog.export_config.* (already split).

Action names to use (RBAC v2):
- auditlog.events.list
- auditlog.events.get
- auditlog.exports.create (kick off export job)
- auditlog.exports.get
- auditlog.export_config.get
- auditlog.export_config.update

Billing actions to exclude:
- billing.* (all)
- invoices.*
- payment_methods.*
- usage.*

2025-03-12 12:05 PT — Rachel Kim (CS) — Asked customer for export details.

Customer response: they only need (1) view audit logs in UI and (2) configure the SIEM export destination; they do NOT need to change retention settings.

They specifically do not want the SecOps user to see invoice totals or payment method metadata in the Console.

2025-03-13 08:51 PT — Marcus Lin (Security Eng) — OK. Proposed custom role definition for Northstar Health:

Role name: "Audit Log Analyst" (customer-facing)
Description: "View audit logs and manage audit log exports. No billing or usage access."

Permissions (allow):
- auditlog.events.list
- auditlog.events.get
- auditlog.exports.create
- auditlog.exports.get
- auditlog.export_config.get
- auditlog.export_config.update

Permissions (explicitly NOT granted):
- billing.*
- invoices.*
- payment_methods.*
- usage.*
- org.settings.update

Implementation approach for Private / air-gapped:
1) Provide a signed policy bundle artifact including this custom role (customer-specific overlay) OR provide instructions to apply a signed "overlay" bundle during upgrade.
2) Customer updates via their installer workflow (no manual edits to on-disk policy files outside the signed artifact path).

I’ll coordinate with Hanae Suzuki + Fatima Noor on the best path for air-gapped package delivery. For now, we can ship them a signed bundle as part of their next scheduled upgrade package.

2025-03-14 10:22 PT — Fatima Noor (Private packaging) — For air-gapped, we can deliver a signed policy bundle as a separate artifact with checksum + signature file. Customer can import during maintenance window using installer hook:
- redwood-installer policy import --bundle rbac-policy-bundle-0.1.2-northstar.tgz --sig rbac-policy-bundle-0.1.2-northstar.sig

We should avoid telling them to hand-edit YAML because it breaks the signature chain and complicates support.

Hanae will confirm the exact command names for their pinned installer version.

2025-03-14 11:40 PT — Hanae Suzuki (Security/Private) — Confirmed on 2025.02.2 Private installer, the supported flow is:
- redwood-admin policy-bundle install --path <bundle.tgz> --signature <bundle.sig>
- then restart control-plane + console-backend pods (rolling) OR run redwood-admin policy-bundle activate (which triggers reload).

We should also remind them to export a snapshot of role assignments before applying.

Also: make sure audit logs include policy_version for the decision (their auditors will ask).

2025-03-17 09:03 PT — Owen Phillips (Support) — Sent customer guidance + proposed role definition for review. Customer confirmed naming and permission intent is correct. They requested the signed bundle artifact rather than editing files.

Coordinated delivery with Solutions Engineering via their secure transfer process for air-gapped updates.

2025-03-18 16:18 PT — Marcus Lin (Security Eng) — Resolution:
- Delivered signed RBAC policy bundle overlay containing custom role "Audit Log Analyst" (no billing/usage permissions) for Northstar Health.
- Provided installation steps for 2025.02.2 Private installer and recommended verification:
  1) Create test user + assign "Audit Log Analyst"
  2) Confirm Audit Log screens load + SIEM destination can be configured
  3) Confirm Billing nav and billing endpoints return 403 with reason code PERMISSION_DENIED
  4) Confirm audit events include actor, role_ids, and policy_version for export actions

Follow-ups:
- Product: track first-class custom roles UX for Private (customer asked for UI-based role editor).
- Security: ensure role matrix doc calls out "audit log export" as separable from billing (avoid future confusion).

Marking Resolved; will close after customer confirms on their next maintenance window.

2025-03-18 16:26 PT — Rachel Kim (CS) — Customer confirmation received: tested in staging cluster (their internal) and separation-of-duties requirement is met. They’ll roll to production during the weekend maintenance window.

Closing ticket.
resolution: Provided customer-specific signed RBAC policy bundle overlay defining custom role "Audit Log Analyst" that permits audit log viewing + export configuration while denying billing/usage access; customer validated in staging.
customer_facing_response: We can support a dedicated "Audit Log Analyst" role for your Private deployment that can view audit logs and manage audit log exports/SIEM destination configuration without granting any billing or usage permissions. We provided a signed policy bundle overlay for your air-gapped environment and installation steps compatible with your current installer version. After applying, you should see audit-log functionality working while billing pages and billing APIs return permission denied.
